solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Illegal prospector who risks landing in kangaroo court? (5-6)

annotation.definition: Illegal prospector who risks landing in kangaroo court?

blocks.note: a miner who seizes ground another prospector has already staked out

blocks.clueFragment: who risks landing in kangaroo court?
blocks.note: read as rough frontier justice, and also as a hopper coming down among kangaroos

annotation.surface: A gold-rush outlaw facing rough frontier justice.
annotation.walkthrough: A kangaroo court is an unofficial, rigged trial, the kind a mining camp held for claim thieves; the kangaroo also nods at the 'jumper' half of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Jumping a claim meant grabbing a mining plot someone else had staked, so the phrase names the offence and the offender at once.

entries.clue: Sign of cold in Gulf state, reportedly (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: Qatar, on the Persian Gulf, said as 'ka-TAR'

annotation.surface: Someone catching a chill in the Gulf despite the heat.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a cold is the last thing you expect in the desert heat of Qatar.
annotation.definitionFit: Catarrh is the mucus that clogs nose and throat, a symptom you show when you have a cold.

entries.clue: Damper yield now and then — it’s a time for showers (5)

indicatorNotes.now and then: something done now and then happens at intervals, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of dAmPeR
the second and fourth letters of yIeLd

annotation.surface: A wet month's harvest is poor, since spring brings showers.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's rain theme hides that 'Damper yield' is only raw material for the letter picking.
annotation.definitionFit: The month is proverbially showery in Britain, hence the saying about April showers.

entries.clue: Piece on daughter, a right-winger, allowing no alternative (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next, so MAN comes first

blocks.note: a chess or draughts piece is a man
standard abbreviation
used literally
a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A newspaper article about a daughter who has turned conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' reads as a written article, but it is a man on a chessboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A mandatory rule is compulsory, so it leaves you no alternative but to comply.

entries.clue: With capsized dhow sunk, mystery becomes flat (4)

indicatorNotes.capsized: a boat that capsizes is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.sunk: the rearranged boat goes down and vanishes from the word

blocks.note: a whodunit is a murder mystery
DHOW jumbled, removed from the front of WHODUNIT

annotation.surface: A sailing boat goes down and a mystery is solved in the calm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like calm water after the sinking; it is a flat you live in.
annotation.definitionFit: Estate agents call a flat a residential unit, one self-contained dwelling in a building.

entries.clue: Hour in post office with bill, big beastly thing where fewer and fewer calls are made (5,3)

annotation.definition: where fewer and fewer calls are made

indicatorNotes.in: the hour is placed in the post office, its letter sitting inside the two-letter abbreviation

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
a neb is a bird's bill or beak
an ox is a large animal

annotation.surface: A long, rambling list of errands ending with a large animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like something to pay at the post office; it is a beak. Mobiles have left the red telephone box nearly unused.
annotation.definitionFit: The public call box is a place for making calls, and the mobile has made it ever rarer.

entries.clue: Part of leg I jerked climbing bringing about change unexpectedly (5)

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is a part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing reads the letters upward, reversing them

blocks.note: five letters spanning the end of 'leg', the 'I' and the start of 'jerked'

annotation.surface: A knee-jerk reflex while climbing causes a sudden shift.
annotation.walkthrough: The anatomy is a smokescreen: 'Part of' asks for a run of letters, not a body part.
annotation.definitionFit: To rejig is to rearrange, often a quick reshuffle made at short notice.

entries.clue: Rotten stand-up could be cleaner (7)

indicatorNotes.Rotten: something rotten has fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A comedian bombs and could clean up their act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand-up' is a comedian in the surface and 'cleaner' sounds like cleaner jokes; here it is a cleaning tool.
annotation.definitionFit: A dustpan is a cleaning implement, so a cleaner loosely by function.

entries.clue: Garden tool operated noisily first to expose poisonous plant (8)

indicatorNotes.noisily: the word is to be heard, not read
indicatorNotes.first: the heard word comes before the garden tool

blocks.note: manned = operated, as a machine is manned
a rake is a garden tool

annotation.surface: A gardener works loudly to clear the weeds around a toxic plant.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue names the tool before the sound-alike, and 'first' reverses that order in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The mandrake, a nightshade relative with a forked root, is toxic, an example of the class.

entries.clue: Film director lacking the least elements of style and charisma isn’t an actor anyhow (9)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the named letters are taken out
indicatorNotes.the least elements of: the first letters, the smallest part at the start of each word
indicatorNotes.anyhow: in any old way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder before removal
the first letter of Style, removed
the first letter of Charisma, removed

annotation.surface: A dig at a director who lacks the style and charisma to act.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a jibe, and Quentin Tarantino does famously take cameo roles in his own films.
annotation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino, maker of Pulp Fiction, is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Western wear that sounds like Autry’s? (5)

blocks.note: Gene Autry, the singing cowboy of Westerns

annotation.surface: Cowboy clothing resembling the singing cowboy's outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: Gene Autry was a 1930s Hollywood singing cowboy, so 'Autry's' becomes 'Gene's'.
annotation.definitionFit: Denim trousers were the working clothes of the American West, and so are Western wear.

entries.clue: Look in study for stock again (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the look is put in the study, the short word sitting inside the longer one

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
lo! = look!

annotation.surface: Checking a study to restock the shelves.
annotation.walkthrough: READ for study is British university usage: you read law at Oxford.
annotation.definitionFit: Loading means filling or stocking up, and the prefix makes it a second time.

entries.clue: Well-heeled in more ways than one? (6,2)

annotation.definition: Well-heeled in more ways than one?

blocks.note: the everyday sense is wealthy, and the literal one is wearing good heels
tells you to take both senses at once

annotation.surface: Someone who is both rich and smartly shod.
annotation.walkthrough: Wedged up is British slang for loaded with money, and wedge heels literally lift the wearer up.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for rich and can be read as raised on wedge heels, so it covers both senses of well-heeled.

entries.clue: Women’s party by North London suburb (6)

indicatorNotes.by: placed next to, so N follows

blocks.note: a hen do is a bride's party with her female friends
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A bachelorette party somewhere in north London.
annotation.walkthrough: A hen do is the British bachelorette party. 'North' belongs to the wordplay, not the suburb.
annotation.definitionFit: Hendon, in north-west London, home of the police college, is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Collision narrowly avoided where keen learners congregate? (4,4)

blocks.note: the standard phrase for an accident that almost happened
keen pupils sit close to the teacher, addressed as Miss

annotation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into two words: near Miss, at the front of the class.
annotation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident that nearly became a crash, and read as 'near Miss' it is where eager pupils sit.

entries.clue: Firm kiss by lover for keeper of course (8)

indicatorNotes.by: placed alongside, one piece after another

blocks.note: Co. = company
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
a swain is an old word for a suitor

annotation.surface: A romantic kiss that's par for the course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeper of course' is a steersman: the cox keeps a rowing boat on its course.
annotation.definitionFit: The cox steers the boat, keeping it on its course.

entries.clue: Vault helps cure invalid (9)

indicatorNotes.invalid: not valid, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A leap that helps heal a sick person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person being cured; it is the adjective meaning not valid. 'Vault' pretends to be a leap.
annotation.definitionFit: A burial vault is a stone chamber for the dead, which is what a sepulchre is.

entries.clue: Vine fruit‘s colour originally between copper and brown (8)

indicatorNotes.originally: at its origin, so only the first letter of the word is used
indicatorNotes.between: the letter is placed between the other two pieces

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first letter of Colour
umber is an earthy brown

annotation.surface: Describing the shade of a grape somewhere between copper and brown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vine fruit' suggests grapes; the cucumber also grows on a vine and is botanically a fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: Cucumbers grow on trailing vines and are fruits in the botanical sense.

entries.clue: Egg-layer additionally incorporating a species from the Isle of Man? (8)

indicatorNotes.incorporating: PLUS takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.from the Isle of Man: the Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: plus = additionally
used literally

blocks.clueFragment: species from the Isle of Man
blocks.note: TYPE, a species or kind, docked of its tail like a Manx cat

annotation.surface: An egg-laying creature said to include a Manx species.
annotation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's Manx cat is famously tailless, so 'from the Isle of Man' tells you to cut the tail off TYPE.
annotation.definitionFit: The platypus is one of the few mammals that lay eggs.

entries.clue: Bake tuna pie for yearly visitor (7)

indicatorNotes.Bake: baking transforms the ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Cooking a fish pie for an annual guest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yearly visitor' sounds like a relative coming for dinner; it is an annual flower, planted fresh each year.
annotation.definitionFit: Petunias are grown as annuals, turning up in the garden for one season.

entries.clue: Ranch in Mayo? (6)

blocks.note: a large farm, especially one out West
mayonnaise, something you put on bread

annotation.surface: A ranch out in County Mayo, Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ranch' and 'Mayo' both also name salad dressings, and Mayo is an Irish county too, so the clue looks like a location.
annotation.definitionFit: A spread is a big ranch or farm, and mayonnaise is a spread for sandwiches.

entries.clue: Theatrical assistant that could be Welsh (7)

blocks.note: the backstage helper who gets actors into their costumes
a style of kitchen sideboard from Wales, with open plate shelves above a cupboard

annotation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' pretends to describe the assistant's nationality; it is the name of a piece of furniture.
annotation.definitionFit: A dresser helps actors change backstage, and a Welsh dresser is one kind of kitchen dresser.

entries.clue: Island where French succeeded in retiring (8)

blocks.note: Timor is an island in south-east Asia
où is French for where
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Asking on which island the French managed to retire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like stepping down from work; it means shy.
annotation.definitionFit: Timorous and retiring are plain synonyms for shy and nervous.

entries.clue: ‘Essential Jacques Brel’ I concede is blast from the past (5)

indicatorNotes.Essential: the essence, the letters at the heart of the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the singer's surname, through 'I', into the start of 'concede'

annotation.surface: Admitting that a greatest-hits album of Jacques Brel is dated.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacques Brel was a Belgian chansonnier of the 1950s and 60s, which is what makes him a blast from the past in the surface too.
annotation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from an earlier time.

entries.clue: Trial prompted by political volte-face in capital (6)

indicatorNotes.political volte-face: a switch from right to left, so R becomes L

blocks.note: the Czech capital
R for right swapped for L for left

annotation.surface: A show trial following a regime change in a capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a court case; it means a trouble or affliction.
annotation.definitionFit: A trial here is a hardship to endure, and a plague is a severe affliction of that kind.

entries.clue: Hard work produced by good right back (5)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
aft = at the back of a ship

annotation.surface: A football right-back praised for his work rate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right back' is a football position in the surface; split, it is R and AFT.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang graft is hard labour, as in a hard day's graft.

entries.clue: Sauce made from spun sugar missing the point (4)

indicatorNotes.spun: turned round, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.missing: to be missing something is to lack it, so the compass point is dropped

blocks.note: SUGAR spun round
S for south, a compass point, removed

annotation.surface: Candyfloss that has lost its peak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spun sugar' is candyfloss on the surface. 'The point' is a compass point, here S.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragù is an Italian meat sauce.

entries.clue: Pinched openings to nostrils affecting sinuses, adenoids, lungs (5)

indicatorNotes.openings to: the opening of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

annotation.surface: A doctor's note on a blocked-up patient.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about the nose, which makes it hard to see which word is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pinched voice is thin and tight, which is how a nasal voice sounds.

entries.clue: ‘Rock the Casbah’ covers in Skegness? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Rock: to rock is to shake up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Cover versions of the Clash song played at a seaside town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests cover versions of the Clash song; they are headwear. Skegness is an English seaside resort, and Skegness rock is the seaside sweet.
annotation.definitionFit: Beach hats are what cover your head at a seaside resort.

entries.clue: Conservative reprobate with universal support backing volatile chamber (11)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so ROTTER, U and BRA are reversed together

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a rotter is a cad
U is the film certificate for all ages
a bra is a support garment

annotation.surface: A Tory cad propped up by all and sundry in an unstable House.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Volatile chamber' reads as a rowdy parliament; it is the engine part where volatile fuel mixes with air.
annotation.definitionFit: A carburettor is the engine chamber mixing air with volatile fuel.
